compute.note: Table I gives the per-experiment GPU (A100), hidden dimension d_h = 200, N_s = 200 samples per iteration and 10^5 minSR iterations for the 10×10 OBC Heisenberg run; 'a single GPU' is the paper-wide statement. No parameter count stated (2D GRU cell with d_h = 200). No wall-clock stated in text for this run: Fig. 3(a) plots V-score versus time in seconds but no total is printed; the 24-hour equal-training-time control in Fig. 5(a) is a separate scaling study with d_h = 100. Hyperparameters tuned with Optuna/TPE (tuning cost not stated). || route2b-pass 2026-09-24: parameters = 5 d_h^2 + 18 d_h + 2 = 203602 for d_h = 200: W_u, W_r (d_h x (d_h + 4) each), W_h (d_h x d_h), W_in (d_h x 4), U_1, U_2 (d_h x d_h each), biases b_u, b_r, b_h, b_in (d_h each), softmax head U (2 x d_h) and c (2); positive RNN (Marshall sign applied), no phase head. Size-independent (one cell for all sites). The code repo (github.com/werro40/RNN-Natural-Gradients @ 63f64a2, README 'Under construction!') implements a different cell (flax GRUCell on concatenated neighbour states, a (2d_h x d_h) U, a GLU output layer) and its Heisenberg-2D.py calls a StackedRNNModel it never defines, so it is not the run code; its config_h2d.yaml has numsamples_per_batch 50 vs N_s = 200 in Table I. Count follows the paper's equations.
